newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares fall on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares fall on profit taking.

text.p: Israeli shares closed lower across the board in another session of profit taking, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares fell 3.22 points, or 1.69 percent, to 186.77 on an all-share turnover of 63 million shekels against 71 million on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 index lost 1.67 percent to 195.78.

"Nothing is logical in this market. Nothing new happened and there was no reason for today's fall beside the fact that a few investors took profit. The market rose too fast and gained more than 10 percent in only two weeks," said Noam Braverman at the Central Securities Corp.
"In the next few weeks activity will remain low as many investors go on vacation because of the Jewish (New Year) holidays and I think the market will not move much," Braverman said.

Makhteshim Chemical Works dropped 4.25 percent to 1,780. On Monday its parent Koor Industries announced it will join Makhteshim and Agan Chemical Manufacturers under a new holding company. Traders said the change will not benefit shareholders.
Koor Industries, the third-most active share, fell 1.0 percent to 27,403 on volume of 2.7 million shekels.
"The trend was negative during the day. We saw some profit taking but investors also realise now there was no reason for the market's sharp rise last week," said Danniella Finn at Batucha Securities.

The most active shares were Poalim Capital Markets and Investments, which gained 1.0 percent to 11,147 on volume of 3.2 million shekels and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which fell 1.25 percent to 116,408 on turnover of 3.0 million shekels.
($1 = 3.17 shekels) - Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211
